name: Mahindra Logistics Ltd
title: Mahindra Logistics Ltd - 540768 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 25.4 cr (INR 21.4 cr ex tax-refund interest) on 23% revenue growth; contract logistics gross margin diluted 46 bps on start-up and manpower costs, with management guiding Express EBITDA breakeven this year.

summary.headline: Mahindra Logistics swung to Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 25.4 crore from a INR 10.8 crore loss, with consolidated revenue up 23% to INR 2,003 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to INR 2,003 crore and reported EBITDA rose to INR 115 crore from INR 76 crore. Adjusted (Ind AS 116) EBITDA was INR 57 crore, up 76% YoY, at 2.8% margin. PAT of INR 25.4 crore includes INR 4 crore of interest on income tax refund, so operating PAT was about INR 21.4 crore. Contract Logistics gross margin was diluted YoY by start-up costs, manpower shortages and minimum wage revisions, while the Express business reached a positive gross margin and narrower EBITDA loss.

segments.name: Contract Logistics (3PL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,623 crore, +26% YoY; gross margin diluted about 46 bps YoY due to manpower shortages, site ramp-up and minimum wage revisions, offset by overhead efficiencies. EBITDA margin rose to 6.9% from 6.6%.

segments.name: Express (MESPL / Rivigo B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 152 crore, +58% YoY; gross margin 6% vs -3.8% in Q1 FY26 and about 4.8% in Q4 FY26 per analyst. EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 1.6 crore; management targets EBITDA breakeven in FY27 and PAT later.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 111 crore, +38% YoY, driven by B2B client expansion (majority of segment is B2B employee transport). Management cites historical 9-10% gross margin target for the segment; adjusted EBITDA margin in the 2-3% range.

segments.name: Last Mile Delivery
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 16% YoY as a deliberate move away from low-margin sites; gross margin rose from 5% to 9%, and the business remains EBITDA positive.

segments.name: Freight Forwarding
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 45 crore vs INR 74 crore, down 39% YoY, due to customer attrition during transition and macro disruption; gross margin about 10% and EBITDA positive.

guidance_outlook: Express business: target EBITDA breakeven in FY27; management declined to specify quarter, citing 'a lot of work to do'.
Medium-term gross margin expansion of 150-200 bps for the overall business, reiterated by CFO.
White space reduction: on track to cut the 1.6 million sq ft white space (as of Q1 FY26) by 95% by September 2026.
Q2 seasonality: heavy rains may hurt Express operations in Q2, with festive demand expected to lift Q3.

Start-up costs from rapid site additions (about one new site a week) expected to normalise over 3-4 months; roughly half of YoY gross margin dilution attributed to this, which CFO said should reverse as the year progresses.
Fuel pass-through: about 80% of B2B Express customers have accepted fuel escalation; remaining pass-through still in progress.
ROCE expected to be shared at H1 results; management said it is 'much healthier' than a year ago. No formal ROCE guidance.
capex_capacity: Warehousing space approximately 21 million sq ft (CFO confirmed); YoY increase reflects new warehouses capitalised, which lifts depreciation under Ind AS 116.
Management does not disclose overall warehouse utilisation, describing it as 'very high'.
Large new site at Luhari near Gurgaon (about 2 lakh sq ft) for a marquee customer, expected to normalise in 3-4 months.

Airport taxi (Alyte) strategy: withdrawing from Mumbai Airport as it did not meet internal profitability threshold; doubling down on Delhi Airport and preferred taxi partner at Noida International Airport, scaling with flight additions.
Company is opening roughly one new site per week due to sales wins above plan.
demand_pricing: Contract Logistics growth driven by M&M auto and farm businesses plus e-commerce, manufacturing and telecom verticals; management won more business than its aggressive internal stretch plan in Q1. Wallet share with M&M not quantified; M&M share of revenue was about 60%, down from close to 70% three years ago, and management says it has no target for this ratio.
Express: management won't disclose volume (tonnage) or split of volume vs yield growth, saying it is prioritising yield; new wins are priced above internal threshold yield.
Fuel escalations with M&M passed through within 24-48 hours; INR 8.10 fuel increase recovered in that window. Contract renewals run on staggered 1, 3 and 5-year cycles.
Freight forwarding lost volumes from some key customers in the transition period; leadership team strengthened.
Mobility margin differs by mix: chauffeur/on-call business is more lucrative than employee transport, where MLL is heavily weighted; limited operating leverage at current scale.
Management described new wins as hard-fought against national RFQs, competing on price, quality, solutioning and Mahindra governance.

qa_highlights.question: Will Express EBITDA breakeven arrive by Q2, and what are Express volumes in tonnage?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes not disclosed; volume and yield both improving. Target is EBITDA breakeven this year, with no quarter specified.

qa_highlights.question: Where can Mobility margins go given revenue near INR 110 crore per quarter and 2-3% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical gross margin of 9-10% is the target. Margin gap vs peers attributed to heavy employee transport mix and lack of operating leverage at current scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Contract Logistics gross margin contract, and is 7% the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Three factors: start-up costs from opening a site almost every week, ad hoc manpower hiring, and lagged fuel pass-through. About half of the YoY dilution is start-up cost, which should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Express EBITDA loss narrow only INR 1 crore sequentially when gross margin rose about 120 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Ad hoc manpower in Q1 was a one-off headwind that has since stabilised; fuel pass-through for B2B tail customers (about 80% done) also lagged, so benefit should flow through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise YoY when warehouse space fell?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO clarified that white space fell, not total warehousing space, which rose. Depreciation increase reflects new warehouses capitalised; sequentially it is broadly flat.

qa_highlights.question: What percentage of business comes from Mahindra and is it a target?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60%, down from close to 70% three years ago. Management says it is not a target and it does not monitor the ratio.

risks_watch: Contract Logistics gross margin (about 6.9% EBITDA, gross margin down YoY): whether start-up costs and wage inflation reverse in Q2 and FY27.
Express EBITDA breakeven target for FY27 remains unquantified; watch Q2 monsoon disruption and whether EBITDA loss narrows further.
Freight Forwarding revenue down 39% YoY; watch recovery of customer pipeline after attrition and geopolitical headwinds.
Concentration: about 60% of business from Mahindra Group, with an M&M-led growth engine.
Fuel and minimum wage pass-through lags; B2B Express fuel pass-through still incomplete (about 80% of customers).
Non-recurring INR 4 crore interest income on tax refund inflated Q1 PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround and FY27 Express breakeven target, but evasive on volume, yield split, customer margins, utilisation and ROCE, which management declined to disclose. Margin dilution in Contract Logistics was explained as temporary start-up and wage costs.
key_quotes: Our objective is not to scale for the sake of scale only, but go for intelligent scale, where every customer, every contract and every investment contribute meaningfully to our long-term profitable growth.
I can pick up the volume as much as I want if I don't care about the yield.

So there is no particular time. All I can tell you is that these are continuous discussions that any supplier or any partner has with the customer across the industry, and we continue to follow the same practices.
